sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:61

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:61:1
items.html: Only the lower half of the light of Tifferet was raised, for the upper half remained in its place: That is, after the screen of the Chazeh was refined and rose to its root in AVI, then through its inclusion in the coupling of the Rosh [head] from there, the Rosh of YESHSUT came out upon it, and from the look of their eyes their Guf [body] expanded from above downward into the two thirds of Tifferet that are from the Chazeh downward. And after the vessel of Tifferet broke and descended to Keter of Beria, this light that was in the lower two thirds of Tifferet was then raised, and it rose to the new vessel of Tifferet, which was made from the posterior of Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:61:2
items.html:
The upper half remained in its place: That is, it did not descend from its degree because of the breaking of its vessel. The reason is what the ARI writes above (page 521, item 44), that the posterior of Aba and likewise the posterior of Ima descended before there was any flaw or diminution in the Yesodot of AVI. For after the posterior of AVI had already descended and they had returned to back to back, the fourth king, which is the upper third of Tifferet, began to reign; and he writes the reason there, that it is because Yesod is entirely anterior and has no posterior that could descend from it, study it there well. And in the Inner Light there it was explained that all this light that came down through the coupling of the Yesodot of AVI is the phase of back to back, since they coupled after they had returned to back to back, and the illumination of back to back is counted as the phase of the anterior of Aba and Ima, that is, from what they have from the beginning of their emanation, in which the matter of the breaking of the vessels causes no harm at all, see there. Thus the light of the upper third of Tifferet down to the Chazeh, which is drawn from the coupling of the Yesodot of AVI, has no flaw whatsoever from the breaking of the vessels, since it is drawn from a coupling of back to back. And this is what he says here: “That the light of the upper half of Tifferet stands in its place, and its taste did not change, and its power in it is strong,” as explained.
And one should not ask, according to this, why the vessel of the upper third of Tifferet broke, seeing that there was in it only from the phase of back to back, which is entirely the phase of anterior, as explained. For the ARI has already written that only in AVI did the phase of the anterior remain in them, whereas in the vessels of ZAT the phase of the anterior broke in them as well. In truth, however, its breaking was not great; rather it descended from the phase of Rosh [head] of Tifferet to the phase of VAK of Tifferet, that is, to the phase from the Chazeh downward. And what the ARI writes above, that it fell into Keter of Beria, is after the Guf of the look of the eyes of YESHSUT expanded in it and it broke, and the light was raised to the upper half of the new vessel of Tifferet — it then fell into Keter of Beria, that is, into the phase that corresponds to it there, for the Guf of YESHSUT that expanded in it is likewise the phase of Keter of YESHSUT, as written above, and therefore it fell into Keter of Beria. From this you see that its breaking was not great, for all the vessels of the kings descended to the ZAT of Beria, and only Tifferet fell into the Keter of Beria, which is close to Atzilut.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:61:3
items.html:
The light of Daat, which descended, etc., it too was raised and rose to its place: It has already been explained above (in the Inner Light, page 538, the passage beginning “The light of Tifferet”) that immediately after the expansion of the three lines of KHB into the phases of the new vessels of HGT, all the lights of the four kings, Daat and HGT, rose together to their place, each one in its own line, study it there well.
And the reason for their rising back to the new vessels of HGT that had come out in their place is the force of the new coupling, which is the Rosh [head] of YESHSUT that came out there in their place. This is the phase of the second expansion, which returns and fills the vessels and the records that remained after the departure of the upper Partzuf, in the manner that was in the previous Partzufim of AK, for the records and the empty vessels of the upper Partzuf always pass over to the Partzuf below it. And so it is here with YESHSUT, which fills the vessels and the records of the Guf of the upper AVI, except that the vessels had already broken and fallen, so that it fills the records alone — these being the lights of HGT that had earlier fallen to NHYM of Atzilut. Therefore they now returned to their place and are filled with the light of YESHSUT, as explained.
By this you will also understand the reason for the double descent that befell the vessels of those kings, Daat and HGT. It is that the essential vitality of those vessels that fell into KHBD of Beria is their records; and since these records were from the phase of GAR of ZAT, which are the lights of the Gufim of the upper AVI, as above, they too fell into the phase that corresponds to them, into the GAR of Beria, that is, into KHBD of Beria. Therefore now, after their records rose into the place of the new vessels and were renewed by the illumination of the Rosh of YESHSUT, on the one hand they gained much, for they attained a new light in place of the first light of the upper AVI that had departed from them; but on the other hand they lost much, for since they became receivers of the light of YESHSUT, they thereby descended from the phase of GAR to the phase of ZAT, since YESHSUT with respect to AVI are only the phases of ZAT, as above. Consequently their vessels that are in Beria are found to have likewise descended from the phase of GAR of Beria to the phase of ZAT of Beria, and therefore they fell a further fall, from the place of KHBD of Beria to the place of NHYM of Beria.
And one should not ask that according to this they should have fallen to HGT of Beria and not to NHYM. For this has already been explained: that in empty vessels the coarseness is regarded as lowliness, and whichever is more refined is the more important among them. Therefore, when HGT and NHYM fall to ZAT, they are inverted, so that HGT fall into NHYM, and NHYM, which are more refined, fall into HGT of Beria, as above, and this is simple.
And know that this light of Daat that rose to its place is only the records of the Hassadim of Daat, but the record of the Gevurot still remained there in Malchut, and it rose only after the breaking of the vessels of the kings NHYM, as written below.
